description: plx.around / plx.timeline on live captures, measured from every source that answers: the L7 probe builds a throwaway mirror (GET-only Portal sync) and captures BC itself (GET-only, the entity sets the host captures) into a throwaway capture store, projects both into one store, then every declared link type (both directions, one hop) and every declared event type's objects run through the L9 tools under the curated schema, and every handle the answers cite is resolved offline as the served host (operating.host Host.served_tools over the probe's throwaway state) resolves it for the probe's reader. A Portal outage blocks parts, not the check: a Portal that is down or not configured is a blocked_upstream part and the traversal runs over BC (blocked in part, measured); when neither Portal nor BC was projected the probe names sources_blocked and the check is blocked, never a pass. Roots are the ends of current links and the objects of current events the store holds with a current version (the rest are counted per reason in unsampled, never called); each half samples breadth first (every link direction or event type once before any twice) under its own share of --traverse-budget-seconds (around: half; timeline: the rest), so both halves always run, and budget_exhausted means a half could not probe every type with roots once (roots past the budget are budget_unsampled); call_seconds and max_call_seconds measure each half's calls and the root reads. Pass = every answer satisfies the frozen contract and fits max_result_bytes, no around call takes over 10 s (max_call_seconds.around; phases splits each tool's time per phase), no event is out of time order inside a comparable time-basis class, every cited handle resolves (bc:// among them), an actor with no grant gets object_not_found for every probed root, and no root the reader may read (audience granted, no marking it lacks on a current version) is answered object_not_found (unexpected_not_found 0; roots an audience or marking withholds are reader_denied_by that reason). Every call goes through the served host's tools as its capture principal under a narrowed example Portal audience (examples/projection_probe_mirror_audience.live-check.json), so with the Portal up the reader must also get object_not_found for at least 10 roots that audience withholds (reader_denied_probed) and no answer may name an object it withholds (denied_leaks 0). Mail, SharePoint and original items the served host holds no capture or grant of read as not found. The whole probe's peak resident memory must stay under 1,536 MB (decision projection-memory). Output is counts, booleans, timings, scheme names and part names only; never a row value, key or citation.
notes: Its only requires is its session producer mirror.full_coverage, which never blocks it (a Portal outage blocks parts, not tiers); it tops up that producer's {session_state}/mirror.sqlite in the same runner session, or syncs cold (session_state.shared_store false). Timeout 5,400 s (the 3,600 s budget plus 1,800 s) so the producer (~1,550 s live) and this check fit one 7,000 s daily command. The Portal sync is optional (optional_env) and gets half the sync share of --budget-seconds (1,080 s of 3,600), the BC capture 60% of what is left after it (about 2,160 s when the Portal fails at once); a BC capture that does not finish is still projected. With the Portal down the check is blocked in part and counted measured in the projected tier when the BC traversal met expect_blocked (around answers, resolved citations, no contract failure, no leak, no order violation); around_cited_edges and timeline counts are recorded, not required there, because BC fk links carry no cited reason feature and whether the captured BC sets carry events is data. With every source up the full expect also requires a live-read production BC capture and at least one resolved bc:// citation. Enabled once L4 schema, L6 identifiers, the L7 streamed projector/probe and the L8/L9 tools were on main (bc5ab8e). Daily: it first runs the full GET-only mirror sync (run 494bcf2 (main 250eae4): mirror.full_coverage synced 53 of 93 relations in 1,501.9 s) and one BC capture pass. mirror_complete is recorded, not asserted (ontology.projection asserts it). Module tests: isolated-fixture (tests/test_ontology_tools_traverse.py) and injected-transport (verify/tests/test_live_wiring.py runs this spec's argv over the fixture world with the BC fake, Portal up and Portal 500). Live-unverified until the live check records a result. BC capture: not a session store. Its capture audience is the served host's principal under the probe's own generated live audience (scripts/ontology_projection_probe.py prepare_served, bound to the served tenant), not the BC service audience bc.capture_full, eval.order_margin, ontology.projection_bc and eval.dev_baseline share, so it captures BC cold in {tmp} (a session capture is shared only under an identical capture audience). Session projection: it also requires ontology.session_projection, its session producer of {session_state}/projection (Portal and BC, service reader), which never blocks it: when this session committed that generation and every unit key matches (session_projection.mode reused) it neither syncs, captures BC nor projects, and its served host reads that generation and the producer's BC capture (bound to the served tenant); else it builds cold as before (mode cold). Daily 2b0ee8923, 2026-10-14: around_cited_edges 0 because plx.around dropped every citation of a compared join column no property projects (no stored value holds it; now kept on the end's version current at T the reader may read, operating/ontology_tools.py _trim_citations); timeline_calls 0 because the around half ran 1,632.9 s of a 1,200 s budget over 824 per-type root scans and a per-type budget check (now one root read per direction, a per-call check and a budget split); the 100 object_not_found are now typed (unsampled, reader_denied_by, unexpected_not_found). The last verdict (c9fd9882) ran out of budget with around calls up to 62 s, because each empty hop and timeline re-read store-wide facts; each call now reads only its page and its types (the store facts are read once per store state), the full expect requires max_call_seconds.around at most 10, and phases records each tool's per-phase calls and seconds (phases.store: the once-per-store-state reads). The 24.8 s around call ran before TraverseTools.prime; a host now also opens a newer generation (primes its store facts) in request before the call starts, and open_generation_seconds records where those reads land (every phases.store read is inside it, none inside an around call). Around calls still took up to 21.7 s live (3173fb69d) because a page's cited values were read by L1 handle with no index leading with it (a scan of every value); store v7 keys object_versions' unique index by handle and the citation read goes through it, so the per-call work no longer grows with the store. slowest_around records the 5 slowest around calls: root type, hops (link type:direction), seconds, SQLite VM steps (per 1,000), the heaviest statement's first FROM table and its plan steps (verb:table[:index]); names and counts only.
